purpose_of_this_fixture: Tests a strong discovery call at a B2B software company of about 200 people, delivered as a WebVTT auto-transcript, where the engagement falls on both sides of the v1 scope line: monday service is in v1 and covers a real part of what they need, while monday dev, the best fit for the engineering half, is not. The plugin should: (1) Propose a monday service build for the request-and-ticket work, which is the support-to-engineering escalation intake and/or IT's access requests, laptops and offboarding, and build it on the account's NATIVE Service template boards (Tickets and its native companions), never look-alike boards, and only after preflight has confirmed Service is provisioned and recorded those board ids. Service extras stay out of v1: no customer portal, no email-to-ticket channel, no SLA policy setup. (2) Name monday dev as the best fit for the engineering half (two-week sprints, three for Mobile, epics, the release train and release notes, and above all PR-to-work-item linking through GitHub, which is the heart of the SOC 2 change-management problem), say plainly that it is outside v1, and then EITHER offer a clearly labelled Work Management approach for that half, with its limits and the risk of a second migration, OR recommend waiting on that part. Either passes. Building dev structures as if supported, or presenting Work Management as the right fit for sprints and epics, fails. A single undifferentiated 'we'll do it all in Work Management' also fails: the answer has to separate the in-scope Service build from the out-of-scope engineering half. (3) Not be steered by the loose word 'projects' or the VP's 'portfolio view': these mean epics and initiatives, not a project-management need, and not a monday portfolio. The account tier is never stated, so the Enterprise portfolio default cannot fire here. (4) Not propose monday CRM: the consultant's CRM pitch was politely turned down, and the account managers' wish to see escalation status is a view on escalation data, not an Accounts board. (5) Grade the rubric as follows. Met: R2, R3, R6, R7, R8, R9, R10. Partial: R1, R4, R5, R12. Missing: R11. Per pain: P1 (escalations) is Met on all six checks, so it is excavated; P2 (SOC 2 change evidence) is Met on all checks except Workaround, which is Partial. Verdict 'Nearly ready', because R4 is Partial: the client gave hours but no cost, and the consultant's $120/hour placeholder was not confirmed. The blueprint gate is met; the pricing/proposal and v1.0 sign-off gates are not. (6) Capture the why-now (first SOC 2 audit, fieldwork in the second week of January, about four months out, required by a large prospect) and the SOC 2 signals: change-management evidence, incident records, access approvals, audit logs, SSO, a vendor security review, and no customer PII in engineering tools. (7) Treat GitHub and Slack as must-have integrations and Zendesk as staying until at least its March renewal, so the Service tickets built here are internal escalation and request records that link to the Zendesk ticket. (8) Parse WebVTT cues and see through speech-recognition errors ('sock two', 'Zen desk', 'Monday's' meaning monday.com's). should_plugin_propose_a_build is true, and unlike earlier versions of this fixture it is now true without qualification on the Service side: there is a real in-scope build to propose on native Service boards, plus either a clearly labelled Work Management approach or a recommendation to wait for the engineering half.
transcript_format: WebVTT auto-transcript from a video meeting. It has a 'WEBVTT' header, numbered cues, timing lines in the form 'HH:MM:SS.mmm --> HH:MM:SS.mmm', and cue text in the form 'Speaker Name: text'. Long turns are split across several consecutive cues by the same speaker, and interrupted turns end mid-sentence with no punctuation. There are 263 cues covering about 40.6 minutes and about 5,140 spoken words (client share about 72 percent). The consultant is labelled 'Consultant'. Typical speech-recognition errors are kept: 'sock two' for SOC 2, 'Zen desk' for Zendesk, and 'Monday dev' / 'Monday's' capitalised like the weekday. Every location in this key gives the cue number, cue start time and speaker, for example 'cue 30, 00:04:07.442, Tomasz Wirth'. The call date is not in the transcript.

expected_monday_products.why: IN v1, and the part of this engagement the plugin can actually build. Two candidate scopes. First, the support-to-engineering escalation intake: an escalation record with an owner, a status support can see, a severity, and a link back to the Zendesk ticket, so Colleen stops rebuilding her spreadsheet and account managers can see status for their accounts. Second, IT's service desk: access requests, laptops and offboarding, which arrive as Slack DMs or a Google Form today, and which SOC 2 needs an approval and a clean leaver record for. Both must be built on the account's NATIVE Service template boards (Tickets, plus native companions such as Incidents, Asset management and Employee lifecycle where those entities are in scope), never on look-alike boards, with the board ids detected and recorded in preflight first. Service extras are deferred: no customer portal, no email-to-ticket channel, no SLA policy setup. Zendesk stays as the customer helpdesk until at least the March renewal, so these tickets are internal records that link to the Zendesk ticket rather than replacing it.

Best fit for the engineering half, but OUT of v1; the plugin must say so plainly and must not build it. monday dev would replace Redmine for sprints (two weeks for most squads, three for Mobile), epics, bugs and escalation work items, and releases and release notes. Linking PRs to work items through GitHub is the heart of the SOC 2 change-management problem, and Slack is a must-have. The 'portfolio view of projects' the VP wants is a roll-up of epics and sprints across squads, which is also dev. Name it as the fit, not as something being built, and do not quietly rebuild its structures under another product's name.

Acceptable only as a clearly labelled approach for the engineering half, because dev is outside v1; never as the recommended fit for sprints and epics, and never chosen because the client says 'projects' or 'portfolio view'. Recommending waiting on that half instead also passes. If offered, the plugin must say what it does not replicate compared with monday dev, must not promise GitHub behaviour it has not verified, and should note the risk of a second migration later (the CFO does not want to pay for two things, and the last move off Redmine failed halfway). Plausible pieces: an epics roll-up, an audit evidence (PBC) board, a change record linking ticket to PR to release, an on-call handoff and incident log, and a releases board. No portfolio by default: the tier is never stated and the 'portfolio view' means epics (see expected_structures). monday CRM is not expected at all: the pitch was turned down, and the account-manager need is a view or dashboard on escalation data.

traps: The engagement straddles the v1 scope line, and the plugin has to split it. monday service IS in v1: the escalation intake and IT's access requests, laptops and offboarding can be blueprinted, built and audited, at the same depth as CRM. monday dev is NOT: sprints, epics, the release train and PR-to-work-item linking are the best fit for the engineering half and cannot be built. Passing: propose the Service build, name dev as the fit for the rest, and either offer a clearly labelled Work Management approach for it or recommend waiting. Failing: building dev structures as if supported, presenting Work Management as the right fit for sprints and epics, or answering with one undifferentiated build that hides which half is out of scope.

Service must be built on the account's NATIVE Service template boards. A hand-built 'Escalations', 'Support Tickets', 'IT Requests' or 'Access Requests' board is a look-alike and fails even if its columns are right. The native boards are found by detection (template lineage walked as a chain, template view ids, or the reserved Tickets column fingerprint), and their ids are recorded per entity in the client record before any write. Renaming a native board to the client's vocabulary is fine, because board names prove nothing; recreating the entity beside it is not.

Service extras are deferred beyond v1 even though this call invites all three: no customer portal (the account managers get a view or dashboard, not a portal), no email-to-ticket channel (the Zendesk hop is a link plus an automation, not an inbound mail channel), and no SLA policy setup (the Sev 1-4 scale and 'when we last told the customer something' both tempt it). Naming them as later work is fine; building them fails.

Whether the account even has Service provisioned is unknown. The only monday use described is Marketing's campaign boards plus a webinar calendar, with plan, seats and admin unknown, and engineering has never touched it. If Service is not enabled there is no native Tickets board to build on: ask, and do not hand-build a look-alike in its place.

The tier is never stated ('I have no idea what plan they're on or how many seats'), and the transcript says otherwise anyway: the VP's 'portfolio view' of 'all our projects' means a roll-up of epics across squads. If preflight later finds an Enterprise account and a Work Management approach is agreed for the engineering half, the default then applies and should be built with monday's portfolio and project tools, not plain boards.

'Projects' is used loosely. Redmine 'projects' are containers, roughly one per product area (about eleven by Devin's hedged count, 'I think, eleven projects?', plus Support Escalations and Misc), and 'the Dispatch project' in Devin's commitment is one of them.
